questions.question:
**Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.**

A. As time passed, he grew jealous of his brother's fine appearance and gentle manners, and at last, he wished to destroy him.

B. When Orlando's father, Sir Rowland de Boys, died, he left his youngest son to the care of his eldest brother Oliver.

C. Oliver however proved an unworthy brother and neglected the boy.

D. It was Oliver who persuaded his brother to wrestle with the famous man who had killed so many others in days past, and it was this cruel brother's neglect of him that made Orlando say that he wished to die.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'BCAD'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• The given sentence is an example of a Sentence Jumble.
 
• We know that the first statement of a sentence jumbled question is usually an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, starting of an incident, or it starts with 'most' or 'once'.&l

questions.question:
**Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.**

Mother said to Megha, “Leave for your office now.”

options.text: Mother said to Megha leave for her office then.
Mother told Megha to leave for your office now.
Mother told to Megha to leave for her office now.
Mother told Megha to leave for her office then.

questions.solution: The correct answer is **'Mother told Megha to leave for her office then.'** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The given sentence is an example of an **imperative** **sentence**. • Let's look at the rules of transformation: • While changing the narration of an imperative sentence, we need to follow the given steps: • The conjunction 'to' should be used in place of a comma (,) and inverted commas (“ ”). • 'said to' will be changed into 'told'. • 'to' is followed by 'V1'. • The second person 'your' will be changed into the third person 'her' i.e. according to the object of the reporting verb. • Lastly, the adverb 'now' will be changed into 'then'. • *Example: * • *The queen said to his servant, "Cook me some delicious food today." (Direct Speech)* • *The queen ordered his servant to cook her some delicious food that day. (Indirect Speech)* • Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is Option 4. ​ Correct Sentence:__ *Mother told Megha to leave for her office then.* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **__Hinglish__** __ • Imperative sentence का narration बदलते समय, हमें दिए गए steps का पालन करना होगा: • Conjunction 'to' का प्रयोग comma (,) और inverted commas (" ") के बजाय किया जाता है। • 'Said to' को 'ordered/ requested/ advised/ urged/ forbade, etc.' में बदल दिया गया है। • 'to' के बाद 'v1' आता है। • The second person 'your' को third person 'her' में बदल दिया जाता है यानी reporting verb के object के अनुसार। • *Example: * • *The queen said to his servant, "Cook me some delicious food today." (Direct Speech)* • *The queen ordered his servant to cook her some delicious food that day. (Indirect Speech)* • इसलिए, ऊपर वर्णित बिंदुओं के अनुसार, हम पाते हैं कि सही उत्तर विकल्प 4 है। [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** • Change in adverbs and determines in Direct To Indirect Speech. **Adverbs(Direct Speech)** **Changed adverbs(Indirect Speech)** Now Then Today That day Here There This That These Those Ago Before Today That day Tomorrow The next day • The following table will enable us to know how tense changes into Indirect speech: **Direct Speech** **Indirect Speech** Present simple (Subject +V1st + Object) Past simple (Subject +V2 + Object) Present continuous (Subject +is/am/are+V1 +ing+ Object) Past Continuous (Subject +was/were+V1 +ing+ Object) Present perfect (Subject + has/have+V3+Object) Past perfect (Subject+had+V3+Object) Past simple (Subject+V2+Object) Past perfect (Subject+had+V3+Object) Past Continuous (Subject +was/were+V1 +ing+ Object) Past perfect continuous (Subject +had been+V1 +ing+ Object) Future simple (Subject+ will/shall+V1+object) Present Conditional (Subject+ would+V1+object) Future Continuous (Subject +will/shall+be+V1 +ing+ Object) Conditional Continuous (Subject +would+be+V1 +ing+ Object) 30:T173a, The correct answer is 'Secluded'.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’.**

It was cloudy in the morning but __the sun is shining__ now.
questions.solution:
The correct answer **'No improvement'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is** grammatically correct**. It does not need any **improvement.**
 
• The **present continuous tense** is used to talk about **actions** and **situations** that are in progress at the moment of speaking.
 
• The following time expressions are commonly used with the present continuous tense: **today, at present, at the moment, still, now, etc.**
 
 
• *Example: The kids are **watching** TV.*
 
 
 
• In the given sentence we are talking about an **action** **taking** **place** at the time of speaking.
 
• Thus we use **the present continuous form of the verb.**
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is **Option 1.**

 ​

**Correct Sentence:__** *It was cloudy in the morning but **the sun is shining **now.* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **__Hinglish__**

__
 
• दिया गया वाक्य व्याकरण की दृष्टि से सही है। इसमें किसी सुधार की जरूरत नहीं है।
 
• **'Present Continuous Tense' **का उपयोग उन कार्यों और स्थितियों के बारे में बात करने के लिए किया जाता है जो बोलने के समय प्रगति पर हैं।
 
• निम्नलिखित time expression आमतौर पर present continuous tense के साथ उपयोग किए जाते हैं: today, at present, at the moment, still, now, etc.।
 
 
• *Example: The kids **are** **watching TV.***
 
 
 
• दिए गए वाक्य में हम बोलने के समय होने वाली एक क्रिया के बारे में बात कर रहे हैं। इस प्रकार हम क्रिया के वर्तमान निरंतर रूप का उपयोग करते हैं।
 
• इसलिए, ऊपर वर्णित बिंदुओं के अनुसार, हम पाते हैं कि सही उत्तर **विकल्प 1** है।

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

__
 
• The following phrases are followed by past indefinite/simple tense:

 
 
• It's high time, It's Time, It's about time, etc.

 
 
• Example: *It's high time I started preparing for the exam in Hindi Literature.*

questions.question:
**Given below are four sentences in jumbled order. Pick the option that gives their correct order.**

A. The robber demanded all his valuables or threatened to kill him.

B. But he put up a brave front and challenged the robber.

C. A merchant was confronted by a highway robber.

D. The merchant was scared to death.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'CADB'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is an example of a Sentence Jumble.
 
• We know that the first statement of a sentence jumbled question is usually an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, starting of an incident, or it starts with 'most' or 'once'.
 
• Sentence **C** in the given question is** the starting of an incident.** It tells us that the **merchant** was **attacked** by a highway **robber**.
 
• **Sentence A** will be the next sentence because a robber always demands money/ valuables from the person he confronts. 
 
• **Sentence D** will be the next sentence because it is connected with **Sentence A.**
 
• Lastly, **Sentence B** will be used.
 
• Thus, the sequence becomes:
 
 
• **C**: A merchant was confronted by a highway robber. 
 
• **A**: The robber demanded all his valuables or threatened to kill him.
 
• **D**: The merchant was scared to death.
 
• **B**: But he put up a brave front and challenged the robber.
 
 
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is **Option 1.**

 ​

**Correct Sequence:__** *A merchant was confronted by a highway robber. The robber demanded all his valuables or threatened to kill him. The merchant was scared to death. But he put up a brave front and challenged the robber.*

__
 
• The given sentence is in Active Voice. As per the given question we have to change it into Passive Voice. 
 
• The structure of the given sentence as follows:
 
 
• Subject + V2+ Object. (Active Voice)
 
• Subject (objective case)+ was/were + V3 + Object (subjective case). (Passive Voice)
 
 
 
• *Example:*
 
 
• *Their cousin showed them some rare photographs. (Active Voice)*
 
• *They were shown some rare photographs by their cousin. (Passive Voice)*
 
 
 
• The subject of the given sentence is 'A traffic policeman'.​​
 
• The object of the given sentence is 'Taru'. 
 
• The subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject.
 
• And 'fined' will be changed into 'was fined'. 
 
• Lastly, the 'by' preposition will be added. 
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is Option 4.

 ​

Correct Sentence:__ *Taru was fined by a traffic policeman for jumping the red light.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **__Hinglish__**

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the given sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

Employees were given incentives based at their performance.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'based at'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is **grammatically incorrect.**
 
• Here, **'based on'** should be used instead of **'based at'.**
 
• In the given sentence **'based on something'** is** a phrasal verb.**
 
• If you base something on facts or ideas, you use those facts or ideas to develop it.
 
 
• *Example: The film is** based on **a short story by Thomas Mann.*
 
 
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is **Option 3.

 ​**

**Correct Sentence:__** *Employees were given incentives **based on** their performance. *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **__Hinglish__**

__
 
• दिया गया वाक्य व्याकरण की दृष्टि से गलत है।
 
• यहाँ **'based at' **के स्थान पर** 'based on' **का प्रयोग किया जाना चाहिए।
 
• दिए गए वाक्य में **'based on something'** एक **phrasal verb** है।
 
• यदि आप किसी चीज़ को तथ्यों या विचारों पर आधारित करते हैं, तो आप उसे विकसित करने के लिए उन तथ्यों या विचारों का उपयोग करते हैं।
 
 
• *Example: The film is based on a short story by Thomas Mann.*
 
 
 
• इसलिए, ऊपर वर्णित बिंदुओं के अनुसार, हम पाते हैं कि सही उत्तर **विकल्प 3 **है। 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• What are **prepositions**?

 
 
• Prepositions are function words that indicate how a noun or noun phrase relates to the rest of the sentence.
 
• Some prepositions, such as **in, on, after, or since, **express temporal or spatial relationships.
 
 
• *Example: The library is **on** the north side of the quad.*
 
 
 
• In other cases, the relationship is more abstract and the best preposition to use may depend on the words around it.
 
• These are known as “dependent prepositions,” and they do not follow any clear pattern.
